bill.title: A joint resolution disapproving the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to "Overdraft Lending: Very Large Financial Institutions".

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects overdraft fee revenue and regulatory compliance obligations at very large financial institutions.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would nullify a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule that limits overdraft fees at very large banks. The rule, published in December 2024, requires these institutions to either cap overdraft charges at $5, set a higher justified amount, or treat overdrafts as credit subject to Truth in Lending Act disclosures. If enacted, the resolution would prevent the rule from taking effect, leaving existing overdraft fee practices in place.

bill.title: Falun Gong and Victims of Forced Organ Harvesting Protection Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 506.

industries.rationale: The bill would require financial institutions to block property and assets of sanctioned individuals and entities involved in forced organ harvesting.
The bill addresses organ transplantation practices and could affect medical institutions involved in international organ procurement or transplant tourism.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would impose visa restrictions and financial sanctions on foreign individuals involved in forced organ harvesting, particularly targeting persecution of Falun Gong practitioners. It would require the State Department to identify and report on individuals and entities participating in such practices, and would direct the President to block their property and deny them entry to the United States. The bill also calls for annual reports to Congress on implementation.

plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.

bill.title: A joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection relating to "Prohibition on Creditors and Consumer Reporting Agencies Concerning Medical Information (Regulation V)".
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects lenders' ability to consider medical debt in credit eligibility decisions.
Credit reporting agencies, which include major consumer reporting bureaus, would be affected by changes to what information they may include in reports.
Hospitals and health systems that extend credit or report unpaid medical bills would be affected by whether medical debt appears on credit reports.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would overturn a Consumer Financial Protection Bureau rule published in January 2025. That rule prohibits medical debt from appearing on consumer credit reports and bars lenders from using medical debt when deciding whether to extend credit. If this resolution passes, the CFPB rule would be nullified and the prior framework would remain in effect.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone with a bank account, a loan or savings.

bill.title: ABC Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.

industries.rationale: Streamlined administrative processes for Medicare, Medicaid, and CHIP may affect how providers interact with patients' caregivers and handle eligibility documentation.
Changes to Medicare and Medicaid administrative processes could affect insurers participating in these programs and their coordination with caregivers.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs federal agencies to review and simplify the paperwork and application processes for Medicare, Medicaid, the Children's Health Insurance Program, and Social Security. The goal is to reduce the burden on family caregivers by eliminating duplicative forms and streamlining eligibility procedures across these programs. Agencies must gather input from caregivers and state organizations, make improvements, and report their progress to Congress.

bill.title: Stand Strong Falls Prevention Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Hearings held.

industries.rationale: The bill would promote provider use of fall risk screening and assessment tools, affecting clinical workflows and preventive care practices.
The bill recommends a Medicare pilot program to cover basic home modifications, which would expand covered benefits and affect claims and reimbursement.
A Medicare pilot covering home modifications to reduce falls would create demand for contractors performing accessibility and safety renovations.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would create a federal advisory committee to coordinate falls prevention efforts across government agencies and develop a national plan to reduce falls among older adults. The committee would evaluate existing federal programs, recommend a Medicare pilot to cover home modifications that prevent falls, and encourage health providers to use CDC fall-risk screening tools. The Administration on Aging would report regularly to Congress on progress in reducing falls and implementing the committee's recommendations.

plain.whoItTouches: People on Medicare. Anyone who buys health insurance.

bill.title: Rural Development Hospital Technical Assistance Program Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry.

industries.rationale: The bill directly targets rural hospitals, providing them with technical assistance, training, and support for operational and financial improvements.
The program explicitly includes increasing telehealth capabilities as a development need, which would affect broadband and telecommunications infrastructure providers serving rural hospitals.
The bill addresses acquiring and upgrading health care information systems including electronic health records, which would involve technology vendors and IT service providers.
The program covers technical assistance for constructing, expanding, and modernizing health care facilities, which would involve construction and engineering firms.

bill.plainSummary: This bill formally establishes a technical assistance program within the Department of Agriculture to help rural hospitals (in areas with 50,000 or fewer residents) improve their operations and finances. The program would provide training and support to help these hospitals modernize facilities, expand telehealth, upgrade information systems, and navigate USDA loan and grant programs. Priority would go to hospitals already participating in certain USDA rural assistance programs, and USDA would report annually to Congress on the program's results.

plain.whoItTouches: Farmers, and anyone who buys food.

bill.title: Justice for Victims of Sanctuary Cities Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: State and local governments face new legal liability and compliance obligations regarding federal immigration detention requests.
The bill creates a new private right of action and liability framework, directly affecting litigation practice and municipal legal defense work.
Municipal liability insurers would face new exposure from lawsuits against local governments under the bill's provisions.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would allow victims of certain felonies committed by non-citizens to sue state or local governments that did not comply with federal immigration detention requests. Jurisdictions that accept certain federal grants could not claim immunity from such lawsuits. The bill also provides legal protections to jurisdictions and their employees who do comply with federal immigration detention requests.

plain.whoItTouches: People applying to live here, and their families here.

bill.latestActionText: Indefinitely postponed by Senate by Unanimous Consent.

industries.rationale: The bill would eliminate a fee charged to oil and gas companies for methane emissions above specified thresholds.
Some electric utilities operate natural gas systems that could be subject to the emissions charge this resolution would nullify.

That rule established procedures for charging oil and gas companies an annual fee when their methane and other greenhouse gas emissions exceed certain thresholds. If enacted, the resolution would eliminate these compliance requirements and the associated emissions charge program.

bill.title: Laken Riley Act

industries.rationale: The bill directly imposes new detention mandates on DHS and creates liability exposure for federal agencies, while authorizing state governments to bring suit over immigration enforcement.

The bill creates new grounds for state litigation against the federal government and expands detention requirements, generating demand for legal services in immigration and intergovernmental litigation.

bill.plainSummary: This bill requires the Department of Homeland Security to detain certain non-citizens who are in the country unlawfully and have been arrested for or charged with crimes including burglary, theft, assault on law enforcement, or offenses causing death or serious injury. It also allows state governments to sue the federal government if immigration enforcement decisions or failures—such as releasing detainees, not conducting required asylum interviews, or violating parole limitations—cause harm to the state or its residents, including financial harm exceeding $100.

plain.whoItTouches: People applying to live here, and their families here. People applying to come here, and their families here.

bill.title: Family Farm and Small Business Exemption Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly exempts family farms from asset calculations for federal student aid eligibility.
The bill changes how federal student aid eligibility is calculated, affecting aid distribution and potentially enrollment patterns.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restore an exemption that allows families to exclude the value of their farm or small business (with 100 or fewer employees) when applying for federal student aid. Recent changes to the financial aid application began counting these assets when determining how much aid a student qualifies for, starting in the 2024-2025 school year. The bill would return to the previous policy of not counting these family-owned farms and businesses as assets in the aid calculation.

plain.whoItTouches: Students, and people paying off a student loan. Students, and their families.

bill.title: HALT Fentanyl Act

industries.rationale: The bill changes registration and licensing requirements for pharmaceutical researchers conducting controlled substance research and affects the regulatory classification of chemical substances.
The bill establishes new criminal penalties and quantity thresholds that will affect prosecution and defense of drug trafficking cases.
Universities and research institutions conducting controlled substance research would be subject to the new registration processes and requirements established by the bill.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would permanently classify all fentanyl-related substances as Schedule I controlled substances, meaning they would be treated as having high abuse potential and no accepted medical use. It sets the same criminal penalties and quantity thresholds for fentanyl-related substances as currently apply to fentanyl analogues. The bill also creates a streamlined registration process for researchers studying Schedule I substances and relaxes some requirements for research facilities working with controlled substances.

plain.whoItTouches: People caught up in the criminal law, and victims of crime.

bill.title: Veterans 2nd Amendment Protection Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Veterans' Affairs. Hearings held. Hearings printed: S.Hrg. 119-35.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects the National Instant Criminal Background Check System used by licensed firearm dealers and importers.
Organizations focused on Second Amendment rights and veterans' advocacy have a direct stake in policies governing firearm access for veterans.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent the Department of Veterans Affairs from sending information about veterans or their beneficiaries to the national firearm background-check database solely because they have someone appointed to manage their benefits. The VA could still share such information if a court has found the person to be a danger to themselves or others.

plain.whoItTouches: People who own or buy guns. Veterans and their families.

bill.title: Protecting Access for Hunters and Anglers Act of 2025
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.

industries.rationale: The bill directly affects manufacturers and sellers of lead ammunition by limiting federal authority to regulate their products on public lands.
Manufacturers of fishing tackle containing lead would face fewer potential federal restrictions on their products' use.
Sporting goods retailers selling lead ammunition and tackle would benefit from reduced regulatory uncertainty around these product lines.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent three federal agencies—the Fish and Wildlife Service, Bureau of Land Management, and Forest Service—from banning or regulating the use of lead ammunition or fishing tackle on federal lands and waters. The agencies could still impose restrictions in specific locations if they determine, based on field data from that site, that lead use is the primary cause of a wildlife population decline and the state agrees to the regulation. Certain existing regulations would remain in place.

plain.whoItTouches: People who live near or work on federal land.
